claims.text: In parallelogram ABCD, the opposite sides are equal: AB = CD and AD = BC.
In parallelogram ABCD, the opposite sides are parallel: AB is parallel to CD and AD is parallel to BC.
In parallelogram ABCD, the opposite angles are equal: angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D.
If both pairs of opposite angles of a quadrilateral are equal, the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.
claims.quote: Both pairs of opposite angles of $MNOP$ are equal. Therefore $MNOP$ is a parallelogram.

claims.text: To prove that MNOP is a parallelogram, prove that one pair of opposite angles is equal (angle M2 = angle O2) and then show similarly that the other pair is equal (angle N2 = angle P2).
Two triangles can be shown congruent by the AAS condition, after the equal angles and the equal side have been established, each with its reason.
When two triangles are congruent, their corresponding sides and angles are equal: from triangle CDZ congruent to triangle ABX, CZ = AX and angle CZD = angle AXB.

Results from an earlier congruence can be used as reasons in a later one: angle XAM = angle ZCO is justified by triangle CDZ congruent to triangle ABX, and the other equal parts of triangles XAM and ZCO are justified as proved above.
Vertically opposite angles are equal (written in the proof as vert opp angles =).
After triangle XAM is shown congruent to triangle ZCO, angle M1 = angle O1; since angle M1 = angle M2 and angle O1 = angle O2 (vertically opposite angles), angle M2 = angle O2.
To show angle N2 = angle P2, first show triangle ADW congruent to triangle CBY, then show triangle PDW congruent to triangle NBY.
Each statement in a proof is written with its reason beside it in brackets, for example (given), (AAS), (proved above) or (vert opp angles =).

items.stem: In parallelogram $ABCD$ , the bisectors of the angles ( $AW$ , $BX$ , $CY$ and $DZ$ ) have been constructed. You are also given $AB=CD$ , $AD=BC$ , $AB\parallelCD$ , $AD\parallelBC$ , $\hat{A}=\hat{C}$ , $\hat{B}=\hat{D}$ . Prove that $MNOP$ is a parallelogram. [figure]
solution: Prove that $\hat{M}_2=\hat{O}_2$: In $\triangleCDZ$ and $\triangleABX$ , $\begin{align*}D\hat{C}Z&=B\hat{A}X&&\text{(given)}\\\hat{D}_{1}&=\hat{B}_{1}&&\text{(given)}\\DC&=AB&&\text{(given)}\\\therefore\triangleCDZ&\equiv\triangleABX&&\text{(AAS)}\\\thereforeCZ&=AX\\\text{and }C\hat{Z}D&=A\hat{X}B\end{align*}$ In $\triangleXAM$ and $\triangleZCO$ $\begin{align*}X\hat{A}M&=Z\hat{C}O&&\text{(given: }\triangleCDZ\equiv\triangleABX\text{)}\\A\hat{X}M&=C\hat{Z}O&&\text{(proved above)}\\AX&=CZ&&\text{(proved above)}\\\therefore\triangleXAM&\equiv\triangleZCO&&\text{(AAS)}\\\therefore\hat{M}_{1}&=\hat{O}_{1}\\\text{but }\hat{M}_{1}&=\hat{M}_{2}&&\text{(vert opp }\angle\text{s }=\text{)}\\\text{and }\hat{O}_{1}&=\hat{O}_{2}&&\text{(vert opp }\angle\text{s }=\text{)}\\\therefore\hat{M}_{2}&=\hat{O}_{2}\end{align*}$
Similarly, we can show that $\hat{N}_2=\hat{P}_2$: First show $\triangleADW\equiv\triangleCBY$ . Then show $\trianglePDW\equiv\triangleNBY$ .
Conclusion: Both pairs of opposite angles of $MNOP$ are equal. Therefore $MNOP$ is a parallelogram.

$\begin{align*}\text{in }\triangleDEC\text{ and }\triangleBCF\\C\hat{D}E=F\hat{B}C\quad\text{(proven above)}\\DC=AB=BF\quad\text{(given)}\\DE=AD=BC\quad\text{(given)}\\\therefore\triangleDEC\equiv\triangleBCF\quad\text{(SAS)}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\thereforeB\hat{F}C&=D\hat{C}E\quad(\triangleDEC\equiv\triangleBCF)\\B\hat{C}F&=D\hat{E}C\quad(\triangleDEC\equiv\triangleBCF)\\\text{but }F\hat{B}C+B\hat{F}C+B\hat{C}F=180^{\circ}\text{(sum of }\angle\text{s in }\triangle\text{)}\\\thereforeD\hat{C}E+B\hat{C}F+B\hat{C}D=180^{\circ}\\\thereforeECF\text{ is a str line}\end{align*}$
